claim.pdf_says: 8.7.5.1 Format 1 (simple-relational-operator): the six alternatives 'IS GREATER THAN / IS > / IS LESS THAN / IS < / IS EQUAL TO / IS =' are enclosed in a full-height pair of BRACES — a curly '{' on the left and a curly '}' on the right (verified at 300 dpi on a crop of the figure). There are no vertical choice-indicator bars inside the braces.
claim.markdown_says:
```
⌐                      ¬
| IS GREATER THAN       |
| IS >                  |
| IS LESS THAN          |
| IS <                  |
| IS EQUAL TO           |
| IS =                  |
L                      ┘
```
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6 braces enclose alternatives of which exactly one SHALL be selected, while brackets enclose material that may be omitted. The markdown draws the delimiter with square-corner glyphs (⌐ ¬ L ┘) that read as a bracket/box, not the brace glyphs (⎧⎫⎩⎭) this transcription uses for braces elsewhere (page 215, page 217). A reader of the markdown cannot tell that a simple-relational-operator requires exactly one of the six forms; the bracket reading makes the whole operator optional.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED on every element, and stronger than claimed. (1) PDF glyphs, inspected directly: I rendered page 203 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v203/spec_p203.png) and cropped the left and right delimiters at 4x. Both are unmistakably CURLY BRACES: each has an upper terminal hook, a straight vertical extension, a pronounced MIDDLE CUSP at mid-height (pointing left on the opener, right on the closer), and a lower terminal hook. A bracket has square corners and no mid-cusp. The braces span the full six-row stack. There are no vertical choice-indicator bars inside them — the space between the opener and 'IS', and between the text and the closer, is empty. The claim's reading of the PDF is exactly right. (2) The markdown quote is verbatim: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 8831-8840 match the quoted block character for character (U+2310 top-left, U+00AC top-right, ASCII 'L' bottom-left, U+2518 bottom-right, ASCII '|' for the sides). No misquote. (3) The transcription has a firm, doc-wide two-way convention that this figure violates: braces are drawn with U+23A7/23A8/23A9 and U+23AB/23AC/23AD (455/279/452 and 452/278/452 occurrences); brackets are drawn with U+23A1/23A2/23A3 and U+23A4/23A5/23A6 (~199/229/196). The ⌐ ¬ L ┘ set appears on only 12 lines across 6 pages and belongs to NEITHER convention. (4) Decisive: that anomalous glyph set is used for BOTH delimiters, so it is not merely an ugly brace — it actively conflates them. On page 645 (DIVIDE formats 4 and 5) it renders the identifier-1/literal-1 required choice, which the PDF draws as BRACES. But on page 635 (DELETE) it renders the INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY pair, and I rendered page 635 at 300 dpi to check: the PDF there shows nested SQUARE BRACKETS, not braces. One glyph set, two opposite meanings. (5) Most damning for this specific page: page 217 of the same transcription renders a relational-operator alternative stack of essentially identical shape ('IS [NOT] GREATER THAN / IS [NOT] EQUAL TO / IS [NOT] = / ...') using correct brace glyphs ⎧⎨⎩ ⎫⎬⎭. So the page-203 rendering is an internal inconsistency against the transcription's own handling of the same construct 14 pages later. (6) The normative force is real and correctly stated: 5.2.6.3 Braces — 'Braces, { }, ... indicate that the syntax element contained within the braces or one of the alternatives contained within the braces shall be explicitly specified or is implicitly selected'; 5.2.6.2 Brackets — the enclosed element 'may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted. No default is implied.' None of the six alternatives consists only of optional words (GREATER, LESS and EQUAL are underlined required key words), so no implicit-default escape applies: exactly one of the six SHALL be written. Read as a bracket, simple-relational-operator becomes omissible, which would license a relation condition with no operator at all. I found no other defect on page 203 — 8.7.3, 8.7.4, 8.7.5, 8.7.5.1 and the trailing 'Format 2 (extended-relational-operator):' heading all transcribe faithfully, and Format 2's figure legitimately falls on the next page.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is accurate as written and needs no correction; it can be sharpened in three ways. (a) The defect is not that a brace was drawn with an unusual brace glyph but that page 203 uses an OCR fallback delimiter set (U+2310 top-left, U+00AC top-right, ASCII 'L' bottom-left, U+2518 bottom-right, ASCII '|' sides) that this transcription applies to BOTH ISO metalanguage delimiters: to braces here and on page 645 (DIVIDE identifier-1/literal-1 required choice), and to square brackets on page 635 (DELETE INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY, verified against the 300 dpi render). The glyph set is therefore not decodable at all, not merely mis-cornered. (b) The strongest internal evidence is page 217, where the transcription renders a relational-operator alternative stack of the same shape with correct brace glyphs ⎧⎨⎩ / ⎫⎬⎭ — page 203 contradicts the transcription's own treatment of the same construct. (c) Precise citations: 5.2.6.3 (Braces) and 5.2.6.2 (Brackets), not the parent 5.2.6; note that the braces' implicit-default provision in 5.2.6.3 does not apply because no alternative consists solely of optional words. FIX: replace the eight-line block with the doc's standard brace glyphs (⎧ / ⎨ / ⎩ on the left, ⎫ / ⎬ / ⎭ on the right) and sweep the other 5 pages carrying this fallback set (389, 635, 645, 799) — resolving each to braces or brackets against its own PDF render, since they are not all the same delimiter. Page 799 is additionally corrupt, using U+2310 as a BOTTOM-right corner. Separately noted, not part of this finding: the code fence also drops the PDF's underlining of GREATER, LESS and EQUAL, which per 5.2.2/5.2.3 marks them required versus the optional words IS, THAN and TO; that is a doc-wide code-fence limitation rather than a page-203 transcription error.
